heroHeadline: Taliban IEA Calls Pakistan's Bannu Evidence 'Baseless' on Day 76 — Formal Mutual Incompatibility Exposed as COAS 'Logical Conclusion' Warning Stands
heroSubtitle: On May 12, 2026 (Day 76 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan issued a formal public rejection of Pakistan's May 11 demarche, calling Pakistan's intelligence-backed allegations that the Bannu VBIED attack was masterminded from Afghan soil 'baseless and unfounded.' The IEA's categorical denial — reported by Pajhwok Afghan News — closes the diplomatic loop in the most adversarial possible fashion: Pakistan has presented technical intelligence; the Taliban has formally declared it fabricated. Neither side has a face-saving path forward under current conditions, leaving the non-escalation framework operating through inertia rather than agreement. Pakistan COAS Field Marshal Asim Munir's May 11 warning that the fight against TTP facilitators will continue 'until its logical conclusion' remains the operative Pakistani position. No Urumqi Round 2 date has been set. China is publicly silent since the May 5 Dangam strike. A secondary pressure track emerged as Pakistan's allowance of Iranian military aircraft at PAF Base Nur Khan drew US congressional scrutiny, further complicating Islamabad's multi-front diplomatic environment.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
